surfaceForm: the audit-and-IR obligations of the regulatory framework. It is the principal anchor of NIS2~Art.~23 (incident reporting: 24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification, one-month final report) and of \gls{gdpr}~Art.~33--34 ...
proposedGenericDecision: Present NIS2 + GDPR as instances of the applicable incident-reporting / breach-notification regime rather than as 'the' framework. Frame the named instruments and their fixed deadlines (24h/72h/1-month) as the EU-jurisdiction instantiation; abstract to 'the applicable incident-reporting regime and personal-data breach-notification regime, with their statutory deadlines'.
rationale: NIS2 and GDPR with their exact statutory deadlines bind the document to EU jurisdiction. The 24h/72h/one-month timeline is EU-specific (NIS2 Art.23); a non-EU institution faces a different regime. Stated as 'the regulatory framework' it implicitly assumes the reader is EU-regulated without naming the country.

surfaceForm: the institution becomes \emph{operationally accountable} for the audit-and-IR obligations of the regulatory framework
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the definite-article 'the regulatory framework' (which presumes a single, reader-shared regime) with 'the institution's applicable regulatory framework', signalling that the named instruments below are the worked example for the EU jurisdiction.
rationale: The definite article asserts a single shared framework, which is the core implicit institution/jurisdiction binding. Generalizing the framing makes the named instruments illustrative rather than universal.

surfaceForm: 27001~A.8.15 (logging) and A.8.16 (monitoring activities) ... NIST CSF \textsf{DETECT} (DE) and \textsf{RESPOND} (RS) functions
proposedGenericDecision: Keep. ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF are jurisdiction-neutral international/voluntary standards applicable across institutions worldwide; they are not institution-specific.
rationale: ISO 27001 and NIST CSF are globally adopted voluntary frameworks; citing specific controls/functions is the project's documented evidence-methodology convention, not a localization issue.

surfaceForm: MoUs with the national CSIRT and \gls{nren}-CSIRT where applicable ... at least one exercise has been conducted with institutional CSIRT or \gls{nren}-CSIRT participation
proposedGenericDecision: Largely already generic via the \gls{nren} macro and 'where applicable'. Confirm the glossary 'nren' expands to a role-based definition (National Research and Education Network), not to RESTENA. Keep the role-based 'national CSIRT / NREN-CSIRT / institutional CSIRT' triad as a parameterizable governance topology.
rationale: Assumes a national-CSIRT plus NREN-CSIRT topology, which is jurisdiction-shaped (some countries lack a distinct NREN-CSIRT). Already softened by 'where applicable' and the nren macro, but the named CSIRT relationship slots are localization points. Verify the macro does not resolve to a UL/LU term.

surfaceForm: Patterns reported in NREN community fora and at REN-ISAC indicate that research-intensive institutions ...
location: ch25-wave7-audit-ir-EN.tex / Section: Exit criteria (realworldbox 'Audit and IR practice in research-intensive institutions')
proposedGenericDecision: REN-ISAC is a specific (North-America-rooted) sector information-sharing body. Generalize to 'sector incident-sharing networks (e.g., REN-ISAC, NREN/GEANT community fora)' so the named body is an example, not the assumed forum the institution belongs to.
rationale: Naming REN-ISAC as the reference forum implicitly assumes membership in a specific regional sharing community; a generic reader's relevant ISAC may differ. Low-stakes because already framed as 'reported patterns', but it is a regional precedent presented as the norm.

surfaceForm: brownfield Microsoft-centric ... Microsoft Sentinel ... KQL ... OpenTelemetry collector; brownfield hybrid ... Splunk ...
location: ch25-wave7-audit-ir-EN.tex / Sections: Trajectory brownfield Microsoft-centric (sec:w7-brownfield-ms), Trajectory brownfield hybrid (sec:w7-brownfield-hybrid)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep. These are commercial/technology product trajectories deliberately offered as alternative starting points (greenfield / Microsoft-centric / Splunk-hybrid); they describe technology estates, not the authoring institution's identity, and are explicitly framed as 'for institutions whose ...'.
rationale: Sentinel/Splunk/KQL/OpenTelemetry are vendor-neutral-by-design trajectory options, each conditioned on the reader's existing estate. They do not bind the document to any one institution; removing them would reduce, not increase, agnosticism.
